components.cost_effect: Analysis requires no extra feedback; direct aggregation costs O(N) arithmetic work per trial.
components.goal: Compare master mistakes to each pool member.
components.key_estimate: For u=(1+beta)/2, W_fin<=N*u^M and W_fin>=beta^m_i for every i.
components.name: Total-weight potential
components.operation: Track W=sum_i w_i. On a master mistake at least half of W predicts the wrong label and is downweighted.
components.requires: Binary weighted voting, unit initialization and fixed 0<beta<1.
transfer_checks: Re-establish both potential bounds if feedback, loss domain or update rules change.

variants.cost: Direct implementation obtains N pool predictions and one label per trial, uses O(N) real-arithmetic aggregation/comparison/update work per trial and O(N) stored weights, hence O(NT) aggregation work. Separately charge pool execution and training. No bit-complexity bound is asserted.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Printed p.215 WM definition and footnote 3; protocol p.213; §2 pp.220–221.
variants.name: WM with mistake-triggered updates
variants.output: One binary prediction per trial before label revelation.
public_inputs: Finite pool size N>=1; fixed beta in (0,1); current binary pool predictions.
variants.query_and_update: Compute q_b=sum of w_i over experts predicting b, for b=0,1. Predict the larger-weight label using any fixed deterministic tie rule. After observing label y, only if WM errs, multiply by beta each weight whose expert prediction differs from y. Leave all other weights unchanged; on a correct WM prediction leave every weight unchanged.
variants.requirements: Obtain all N binary pool predictions before the master predicts; observe the binary label afterwards and pass it to the pool. Pool members may learn from previous labels.
variants.state_and_initialization: Set w_i=1 for i=1,...,N. No horizon, best-expert identity or mistake budget is required.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Choose one fixed 0<beta<1 before the run. Run for any finite T trials; no tuning guarantee or terminal optimization step is claimed.
